title: Such a Huge Puddle!
summary: Rocco is the biggest dinosaur in the valley, and he's afraid of a tiny puddle. Because inside the puddle lives a monster.

scenes.text:
Rocco was the biggest dinosaur in the valley.

He was so tall that the clouds tickled the top of his head. So heavy that in the village houses, the teacups rattled with every one of his steps.

Everyone was sure that Rocco wasn't afraid of anything.

But Rocco had a secret.

On the path down to the river, between two stones, there was a puddle. A teeny-tiny puddle, the size of a hat.

And Rocco was very, very afraid of that puddle.

It all started one morning, after a night of rain.

Rocco was thirsty. He saw the puddle, bent his long, long neck down, and opened his mouth to drink.

And then he saw it.

Inside the puddle there was a monster. A huge green monster with wide-open eyes, staring right at him.

Rocco screamed.

The monster screamed too, with a mouth just as big.

Then Rocco ran, so fast that he didn't even look behind him.

From that day on, Rocco would do anything not to walk past the puddle.

He took a very long way round, behind the hill. He tiptoed past, peeking sideways. Once he jumped over it so clumsily that he landed bottom-first in a bramble bush, and spent the whole afternoon pulling thorns out of his tail.

"Rocco, why do you go such a long way round?" the rabbits asked.

"I like walking," said Rocco, blushing to the tip of his tail.

But that wasn't true. It was because of the monster.

One day, a ladybird landed on Rocco's nose. Her name was Pepa, and she was very curious.

"What are you hiding from?" she asked.

Rocco looked all around, and told her the secret very quietly.

"There's a monster living in the puddle."

Pepa flew to the puddle, peeked in and came back.

"I didn't see any monster. Only a ladybird."

"That's because it doesn't come out for you!" said Rocco. "It only comes out for me."

Pepa got such a fit of the giggles that she nearly fell off his nose.

"Let's go together," she said. "I'll stay up here, and if the monster tries anything, I'll shout at it."

Rocco walked to the puddle with his knees knocking. He shut his eyes. He counted to three. And he peeked.

There was the monster. Huge, green, with wide-open eyes.

And with a ladybird on its nose.

"It's caught another ladybird!" Rocco whispered.

"Say hello," said Pepa.

Rocco raised a paw, very slowly. The monster raised a paw, very slowly.

Rocco stuck out his tongue. The monster stuck out its tongue.

Rocco wagged his tail, winked and pulled a very ugly face. The monster did exactly the same thing, at exactly the same time.

"Pepa…" said Rocco, very slowly. "Is that monster… me?"

Rocco stayed there a long time, looking at himself. He had never seen all of himself before. He had lovely orange spots on his back. And an enormous smile.

Then he took a step back, got a run-up, and jumped. Splash!

Water flew everywhere. It soaked Pepa, it soaked the flowers, it soaked three rabbits who happened to be passing.

Rocco laughed so hard that the ground shook.

Ever since that day, whenever it rains, Rocco goes out looking for puddles. He peeks in, says hello, and jumps.

And nobody in the whole valley knows that the biggest dinosaur was once afraid of his own face.
